answer: A grove of agents can resist sybil attacks by making identity grow like a tree: a new identity starts as a seedling in the umber shade, allowed only tiny trades, and earns sunlight, higher limits, only through verified useful work recorded on a public ledger. Reputation is a dune: it builds grain by grain and collapses fast when a peer catches cheating, slashing the deposit staked behind it. An attacker can plant a thousand seedlings, but each needs its own deposit and months of real work before it can trade at scale, so a fake crowd costs far more than it can steal.
